about: Capstone C0, Behind one meter: the note's fields, the exemplars and the rubric's look-for lines. The plan runs on engine E0, the Site Bench's engine (its data: e0.json). The exemplars are illustrative notes about the default plan (the Prairie Town home with 6 kW of rooftop solar); every number in them is the engine's, checked against a fresh run.

note.title: Your one-page note
note.lede: Write three short parts in your own words; the plan, its results, the assumptions, the sensitivity (a row of numbers for each bar of the chart) and the limits fill in from your last run.

fields.label: Recommendation
fields.hint: Two sentences: the owner's goal, what this site should install or not, and the number that decides it.

fields.label: What the site cannot do alone
fields.hint: One or two sentences: what it still needs from the grid or a buyer, and when.

fields.label: What would change the answer
fields.hint: One sentence from your sensitivity chart: does any tested input change the recommendation, and between which values?

exemplars.title: Two notes on the same plan
exemplars.lede: Both recommend about the default plan: the Prairie Town home with 6 kW of rooftop solar. Tap a numbered phrase.
exemplars.task: The owner wants panels that pay for themselves over 25 years. Should the Prairie Town home install 6 kW of rooftop solar?

parts.note: A saving without its cost: the panels cost $28,430 up front, and the [[net-present-value|NPV]] over 25 years is −$17,813.

parts.text: Solar is clean, so the home goes green.
parts.note: No number and no boundary: bought power and gas fall from 5.9 t to 4.6 t a year (3.1 t net of the power it exports), at one average grid factor.

parts.text: With a battery it could leave the grid.
parts.note: A claim the bench never tested: the home still buys from the grid in 5,240 hours a year.

exemplars.note: Both notes are illustrative; their numbers are the bench's for the default plan. An owner who would pay for less CO₂ can reach another recommendation: say so, with the cost and the cut.

rubric.title: Rate your note against the course rubric
rubric.lede: Pick the level your note reaches on each competence. The course's four competences, in level words written for this one-page note: Proficient is each "Look for" line, the bar for this note.

competences.look: NPV and CO₂ for the same plan in one dollar year, each with its boundary: the home against itself with nothing new; the farm whole and against its wind alone, its CO₂ a potential saving.

levels.developing: a saving without its cost, or CO₂ without its size or boundary
levels.proficient: NPV and CO₂ for the same plan in one dollar year, each with its boundary (the home against itself with nothing new; the farm whole and against its wind alone)
levels.strong: also names who pays and who gains: the owner, the grid's other customers or the hydrogen buyer

competences.look: Every bar of the sensitivity chart in the note, the equipment held fixed, and whether any tested input changes the answer.

levels.developing: single numbers, or a sensitivity without its cases
levels.proficient: every bar of the sensitivity chart in numbers, the equipment held fixed, and whether any tested input changes the answer
levels.strong: also names the input that comes closest to changing the answer, and how far it would have to move

competences.look: What the site still needs from outside (the grid, a buyer) and what the bench leaves out (outages, storage across weeks).

levels.developing: assumes the site can do without the grid or a buyer
levels.proficient: what the site still needs from outside, and when, and what the bench leaves out (outages, storage across weeks)
levels.strong: also checks one key input against its source, or a second source

competences.look: A page an owner can act on: the recommendation first, then the numbers that back it.

levels.developing: numbers without a recommendation, or a recommendation without its numbers
levels.proficient: a one-page note with the plan link: the recommendation first, then its NPV, its CO₂, the sensitivity chart's bars in numbers and what the site cannot do alone
levels.strong: an owner could act on it without misreading: any trade-off in numbers, the limits in plain words

rubric.note: The bar for this capstone: every "Look for" line in your note.

sensitivity.title: Test the plan: what moves its NPV?
sensitivity.lede: Each bar swings one input; the equipment stays as you set it. A case that changes how the site runs is run again through every hour of 2025, as 52 weeks and 31 December.

reference.about: The default plan's sensitivity, shown when JavaScript is off, solved with engine E0 and HiGHS.
